class.name: PhysXWaterSurface3D
class.brief_description: A real animated water surface: a GPU FFT ocean spectrum layer plus a local ripple layer that bodies can disturb, rendered as a displaced mesh.
class.description: Two coupled simulation layers, both real-time GPU compute (a private [RenderingDevice], not the CPU): a local iWave-style ripple layer (a damped 2D wave equation you can disturb via [method submit_sphere]/[method submit_impulse]) and a Tessendorf FFT ocean spectrum layer (large-scale wind-driven chop, tuned by [member wind_speed]/[member wind_direction]/[member wave_amplitude]). Both are ported from the caustic-volume reference project's simulation approach, not its full ray-marched photon-caustics renderer -- rendering here is a plain displaced mesh with refraction, not that technique. A child [MeshInstance3D] (a subdivided [PlaneMesh], sized to [member ocean_domain_size]) is created automatically and displaced by both layers, summed. Call [method sample_height] to query the same combined surface on the CPU -- e.g. from a buoyancy script (see [code]demo/common/buoyant_body.gd[/code] in the paired demo project) -- and [method submit_sphere] once per physics tick per floating body so it actually disturbs the ripple layer, not just receives a height back. No [RenderingDevice] compute support (e.g. running headless) leaves the surface flat and [method sample_height] returning [member water_level] plus zero -- a graceful no-op, not an error, matching every other GPU solver in this module. Only runs in an actual running game, never in the editor -- placing or moving the node in the Inspector does not simulate.

method.name: get_caustics_texture
method.description: The rendered caustics light-pattern texture (see [member caustics_enabled]) -- assign it to a floor material's albedo/emission, sampled by world XZ against the same extent as [member ocean_domain_size], to show the pattern. Null until [member caustics_enabled] is true and the node has built (never in the editor, same as the water simulation itself).

method.name: clear_sphere
method.description: Removes a previously-submitted sphere proxy (see [method submit_sphere]) by its owner id. Call this when a floating body leaves the water or is freed; a proxy left in place otherwise keeps disturbing the ripple layer at its last submitted position.

method.name: sample_height
method.description: The combined surface height (ripple + ocean layers, plus [member water_level]) at [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ, bilinearly sampled from the last periodic readback (a few frames behind the GPU simulation -- fine for buoyancy, not meant for sub-frame precision). [code]world_pos.y[/code] is ignored.

method.name: submit_impulse
method.description: A one-shot local disturbance (a splash) at [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ -- consumed by the next simulation step, then cleared automatically. Call it once per event (e.g. on impact), not every tick.

method.name: submit_sphere
method.description: A persistent body proxy that pushes the ripple layer's surface down near [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ, proportional to [code]radius[/code] and [code]strength[/code]. Call once per physics tick while a body is in the water (e.g. from its own [code]_physics_process[/code]), keyed by any id stable for that body's lifetime -- [code]get_instance_id()[/code] works well. Call [method clear_sphere] with the same id when the body leaves.

members.member: World-space Y of the floor the caustics pass projects onto (see [member caustics_enabled]). Set to match the actual floor under the water in your scene.

Enables the cheap grid-projection caustics pass (the technique the caustic-volume reference's `lite` build uses -- a single rasterized draw of the water's own grid mesh, refracted per-vertex onto [member caustic_floor_y], not ray marching). See [method get_caustics_texture].
Damping (ALPHA) on the local ripple layer's wave equation -- higher settles disturbances faster.
Water depth, used by the FFT ocean layer's dispersion relation (shallower water changes how wave speed relates to wavelength).
World-space extent (X, Z) of the local ripple layer -- independent of [member ocean_domain_size], see [member ocean_grid_resolution]'s own note on why.
Cell count per side of the local ripple layer's grid. Not required to be a power of two, unlike [member ocean_grid_resolution].
World-space extent (X, Z) of the FFT ocean layer -- also the size of the rendered [PlaneMesh].

Cell count per side of the FFT ocean layer's grid. Rounded up to the nearest power of two if set otherwise -- the Stockham FFT passes require it. Independent of [member grid_resolution]/[member domain_size] (the ripple layer's own grid) by design: they're two different consumers of "water height" with very different resolution/precision needs, kept architecturally separate rather than forced to share one grid.
Mean world-space Y of the surface -- place the node here rather than relying on its own transform, since the rendered mesh and both simulation layers are displaced relative to this baseline.

The material driving the surface mesh's displacement/shading. A default is created automatically if left unset -- assign your own only if you need to customize the look; it must keep sampling [code]ripple_height_tex[/code]/[code]ocean_height_tex[/code] in its vertex shader the same way the default does, or the mesh will stop moving.

The FFT ocean layer's Phillips spectrum amplitude constant -- higher makes larger waves. Empirically tuned, not a physical unit (see the module's own build notes on the FFT solver for how the default scale was calibrated).
Wind direction (X, Z) driving the FFT ocean layer's wave alignment. Need not be normalized.
Wind speed driving the FFT ocean layer's spectrum -- higher produces longer, larger waves.
